For training the model, a simple neural network called a Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) is used. An MLP is a straightforward but widely used type of neural network. It consists of multiple layers— an input layer, one or more hidden layers, and an output layer—where each layer is made up of units called neurons. In this structure, information flows in one direction – from the input layer, through the hidden layers, to the output layer. Each layer processes the data it receives and passes it to the next layer. The network improves its ability to make predictions, like forecasting stress and strain, by adjusting the connections between neurons based on examples it has seen. UNCLASSIFIED AMMT – 316H SS Los Alamos National Laboratory Page 3-39 The network takes in inputs such as thickness, width, time, build direction, manufacturer, post- fabrication heat treatment, and build parameters, and it outputs predictions for stress and strain. The first hidden layer of the network contains 64 neurons, while the second has 32 neurons. The dataset, which includes information on 214 specimens, is divided into training and testing sets. Data from the remaining 4 specimens is set aside to assess the model's predictive accuracy. The MLP model is trained using the training data, and its performance is evaluated on the testing data. Several hyperparameters, such as epochs, batch size, and learning rate, can be adjusted. Different combinations of these hyperparameters are experimented with to determine their effect on the model's performance. Figure 41 presents prototype results for four specimens, with the ground truth stress-strain curves shown on the left and the model's predictions on the right.
